function.name: view_codebase
function.description:
Read-only viewer for files and directories in the codebase.
Use this tool to READ file contents or INSPECT directory structure.
For Python files, set concise=True to obtain a structural outline (imports, class/function signatures, major blocks).
If the output is truncated or insufficient:
1) Use semantic_search or grep to identify relevant line numbers.
2) Call this tool again with view_range=[start, end].

view_range.description: Line range [start, end], 1-based. If omitted, the entire file will be read. Use -1 as end to read until end of file.

concise.description: If True, return a structural outline for Python files.

python_only.description: If True, restrict viewing to .py files only.

function.name: semantic_search
function.description:
High-level semantic search over the codebase.
Use this tool FIRST to identify relevant files, symbols, or modules related to the question.
The tool returns a summarized list of file paths with match counts.
Set include_lines=True ONLY when exact line-level matches are required.

python_only.description: If True, restrict viewing to .py files only.

max_files.description: Maximum number of files allowed to match.

include_lines.description: If True, include matching line numbers and content (intended for single-file or small searches).

function.name: execute_readonly_command
function.description:
Read-only shell inspection tool for raw repository exploration without context control.
Typical use cases:
- Listing files/directories: ls, tree, find
- Text matching: grep, rg, ag
- Small file snippets: head, tail, sed -n
- Counting/summarizing: wc, sort, uniq
- File metadata: stat, file, du, df

command.description: The bash command to execute (read-only). Must start with an allowed inspection command.
